description: We are a group motivated by creativity, innovation, and our passion for creating meaningful digital products. Our goal is to develop digital products which are not only practical but are also user-friendly. In other words, we aim at developing digital products which are aesthetically pleasing and functional as well.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an educational and fun browser-based game that transforms the history of the space era into an experience of driving through it. The game begins by opening a 3D Solar System where you land either on Mars or the Moon, and proceed to drive a rover or an Apollo Moon Buggy across the big open environment. The historical mission sites are located far from one another, requiring a bit of driving in order to reach them. Mars has 8 historical sites consisting of Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Phoenix and Ingenuity. The Moon has 16 historical mission locations consisting of Apollo landers, scientific stations, roving vehicles parked at particular locations and the Surveyor 3. The player stops at every location, touches the elements of the equipment and reads the story consisting of the timeline and mission status, while getting a source link to NASA.
details:
The game we developed is a browser-based 3D exploration game designed to ensure space-mission history is presented accurately and engagingly. It starts with a stylized view of the Solar System and the user must select either Land on Mars or Land on the Moon. Then he drives a rover or an Apollo-style Moon Buggy in order to find 24 historical sites (eight on Mars and sixteen on the Moon). In the game, the map only specifies a location while a story becomes unlocked once the user drives to the location and inspects the place. Each story includes tappable equipment parts, timeline, mission status, and a link to NASA sources.

There are chunked terrain built using fractal noise, instanced rocks and site models loaded upon approaching the place. The Moon also has a black sky, stars, a static Earth, ballistic dust, low gravity suspension and synthesized sounds but no wind distances are compressed.

Creativity: the process itself is the learning experience, and it dispels many misconceptions (like that only Apollo 15, 16 and 17 had a roving vehicle). Mars and Moon discoveries are organized in a journal; Beyond Mars contains stories about Dawn, NEAR, Pioneer and Kepler. Touch support makes it accessible from a phone.

Tech: JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Three.js (WebGL), Web Audio, Canvas 2D and FFmpeg. Any recent web browser will do.
